title: gov.uk: £16,000 of wages and £200 of interest; the starting rate for savings left after wages is £1,570, so no tax is due on the interest
working: Personal allowance 12,570 is used by wages. Wages above it: 16,000 - 12,570 = 3,430, which reduces the 5,000 starting rate to 1,570. The 200 of interest sits in it at 0%.

title: gov.uk: £1,300 of interest for a basic rate taxpayer; the first £1,000 is covered by the personal savings allowance and £300 is taxed at 20%, £60
working: Other income uses the whole starting rate. PSA 1,000 at 0%. 1,300 - 1,000 = 300 x 20% = 60.

title: Budget 2026: the same £300 of taxable interest is charged at the 24% savings basic rate from April 2027, £72
gov.uk: a higher rate taxpayer has a £500 personal savings allowance; £2,000 of interest on £60,000 of other income leaves £1,500 at 40%, £600
working: Taxable other income 47,430 is above the 37,700 basic rate limit, so the PSA is 500 and the remaining 1,500 is in the higher rate band at 40%.

title: gov.uk: with no other income, the personal allowance, then the £5,000 starting rate, then the £1,000 personal savings allowance cover £18,570 of interest
gov.uk: Scottish taxpayers pay the same tax as the rest of the UK on savings interest
working: Same as the England example: 300 x 20% = 60.
